scenarios.title: Lost update (var++)
scenarios.description: {workers} coroutines increment a shared field: read → yield() → write.
scenarios.expectation: We expect {workers}, but we will see fewer.
scenarios.explanation: There is a suspension point between the read and the write. Other coroutines get to read the same value, so their writes overwrite one another. Note: this happens even on a SINGLE thread — concurrency is not the same thing as parallelism.

scenarios.title: Fix: Mutex
scenarios.description: The same code, but the critical section is wrapped in `mutex.withLock { }`.
scenarios.explanation: The Mutex from kotlinx.coroutines suspends the coroutine instead of blocking the thread. That makes it cheap and safe, unlike `synchronized`, which would block the thread along with the whole dispatcher.

scenarios.title: StateFlow: .value = instead of update {}
scenarios.description: {workers} coroutines run `flow.value = flow.value + 1` with a yield() in between.
scenarios.expectation: We expect {workers}, but we will see fewer.
scenarios.explanation: `.value = x` is a plain write, not an atomic operation. The read-modify-write pattern on a StateFlow is exactly as race-prone as it is on an ordinary field.

scenarios.title: Fix: StateFlow.update {}
scenarios.description: The same code expressed as `flow.update { it + 1 }`.
scenarios.expectation: Exactly {workers} — update runs a compare-and-set loop.
scenarios.explanation: `update {}` retries the lambda until the value is written without a collision. That is why the lambda must be pure and cheap: it may run several times.

scenarios.title: The MVI loop serializes intents
scenarios.description: {workers} coroutines call dispatch() at once; a single consumer reduces them.
scenarios.explanation: This is how MviStore works in this project: dispatch only puts an intent on a channel, and one loop consumes it. Reduction never runs concurrently, so the reducer needs no locks at all.

scenarios.title: collectLatest cancels stale requests
scenarios.description: Five requests fired in quick succession; each one “takes” 50 ms.
scenarios.explanation: This is the mechanism that stops a search field from having fresh results overwritten by stale ones. In this project UsersViewModel relies on it.

scenarios.title: Channel vs SharedFlow for effects
scenarios.description: An event emitted BEFORE any collector had a chance to subscribe.
scenarios.expectation: Channel delivers the event, MutableSharedFlow drops it.
scenarios.explanation: That is why one-off effects (snackbars, navigation) live in a channel rather than a SharedFlow without replay. Otherwise an error message vanishes exactly when the screen happens to be recreating.
